title: Gourmbane, Millet and Peanut Soup
author: Bineta Diallo Dioh
desc: Millet grits and raw peanut flour stirred into three litres of meat, cowpea, dried fish and yet broth, soured with tamarind or lemon.
longDesc: A thick millet-and-peanut soup from the Slow Food/FAO Senegal booklet. Meat, crushed cherry tomatoes, tomato paste, cowpeas, dried fish, yet, garlic, onion and four small toufas boil in three litres of water; millet grits mixed with raw peanut flour are added gradually to avoid lumps, stirring often with a wooden spatula over medium heat, and tamarind juice or lemon is stirred in. The finish is described, not timed: the soup must be neither too compact nor too fluid, and the millet must be well cooked.
ingredients: 50 g dried fermented fish, in pieces
4 small toufas (as printed; not defined in the source)
3 tbsp tamarind juice or lemon juice
Salt and pepper — quantities not printed
steps: Wash the meat, the dried fish and the yet. Mix the millet grits with the peanut flour.
Bring the 3 litres of water to a boil in a deep pot. Add the meat, crushed cherry tomatoes, tomato paste, cowpeas, dried fish, yet, garlic and onion.
Pound or blend as needed, then pepper and salt.
Once boiling, add the millet-and-peanut mixture gradually to avoid lumps. Stir often with a wooden spatula so it does not stick; cook over medium heat.
Add the tamarind or lemon juice. Serve hot.
chefTips: The printed finish is ‘neither too compact nor too fluid’ with ‘the millet grits well cooked’.
Add the millet-peanut mix a little at a time, stirring, or it clumps.
No cooking time is printed. Cook until the millet is soft; 60 minutes is an estimate.
Yet and dried fish are bought, already fermented.
commonMistakes: Dumping the millet in all at once.
servedWith: Served hot, as a meal in itself
healthBenefits: Millet and cowpeas give fibre and plant protein.
culturalNote: The toufa and yet content points to the Saloum and Petite Côte shellfish economy, but the booklet does not say so; that reading is inferential.
sources: Source: ‘produits et plats traditionnels / Sénégal / de la terre à la table’, Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity with FAO; recipes credited to chef Bineta Diallo Dioh. No date printed. Yield: ‘Pour 6 personnes’. TWO-PASS agreed on all quantities.
TIME: no cooking time is printed — both passes agree there is none (pass two: ‘Aucun temps ou température chiffré n’est donné’). Prep and cook times in this entry are estimates.
Cue, short fragment: ‘ni trop compacte ni trop fluide et les brisures de mil bien cuites’.
No region or ethnic group is attributed by the booklet for this dish; placing it in the Sine-Saloum is the editor’s inference from the ingredients.
‘Toufa’ is not defined in the source.
